title: First overview

blocks.what_we_do: Measure missingness before deciding which samples or sites to remove.
blocks.why: Call rate is the fraction of eligible genotypes that are observed; missingness is one minus call rate. A sample report asks whether a well has many no-calls. A variant report asks whether a site fails across many wells. Examine both because these represent different possible failures.
blocks.command:
```{r s2-4}
out <- guided_path(cfg, "2.4", "missing")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "2.2"), "--missing", "--out", out))
smiss <- guided_table(paste0(out, ".smiss"))
vmiss <- guided_table(paste0(out, ".vmiss"))
summary(as.numeric(smiss$F_MISS))
summary(as.numeric(vmiss$F_MISS))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-2_state --missing --out results/guided/s2-4_missing --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--pfile` reads a native genotype prefix. `--missing` writes separate sample and variant missingness reports without filtering. `--out` sets the output prefix; `--threads 2` and `--memory 2048` bound resources. The R helper prints the exact command with your own safe paths.
blocks.expected_result:
A sample report and a variant report; some observations are much worse than the main distribution. No samples or variants are removed at this step.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and available instructor reference counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: A poorly performing well, failed probes or groups of affected samples. A threshold is a decision rule, not a diagnosis of the underlying cause.
blocks.quick_check:
If F_MISS is 0.03, what is the call rate?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

0.97, or 97%.

</details>
